findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk full).
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle or retry.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError::Io> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| PacketError::Io(e))?

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console I/O inside a data-parsing function that should be pure.
findings.failure_mode: Side-effecting shell logic fused into the functional core makes the parsing non-deterministic, non-reproducible, and impossible to test without capturing stdout. Violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell.
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. Move all I/O (file reads, logging) to the imperative shell layer. Core parsing must be a pure function.

findings.problem: parts[0] indexes into a Vec created from split without bounds checking.
findings.failure_mode: Empty line or malformed line causes IndexOutOfBoundsException (panic), crashing the process on hostile input.

findings.problem: parts[1] indexes into split output without bounds checking.
findings.failure_mode: Single-field line (no comma) causes index-out-of-bounds panic on hostile input.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric string (e.g. "abc", "", overflow).
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data crashes the process instead of returning a typed parse error the caller can reject gracefully.

findings.problem: (...parse::<u32>().unwrap()) as u16 performs a lossy narrowing conversion without bounds check.
findings.failure_mode: Values in [65536, 4294967295] silently truncate to u16 range, corrupting data without error. Illegal values become representable.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| PacketError::Overflow("value exceeds u16 max"))?

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper — every internal error is a panic.
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot distinguish between IO failure, parse error, overflow, or allocation failure. All manifest as panics.
findings.fix: Declare pub fn load_packets(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError> with an enum covering Io, Invalid, Overflow, and Allocation variants.

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String — no domain invariants, no newtype, no smart constructor.
findings.failure_mode: Empty, whitespace-only, or otherwise invalid names are silently accepted. The domain has no protection against illegal name values.
findings.fix: Use a Name newtype struct with a smart constructor that validates non-empty/trimmed input, or use NonEmptyString from a crate.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates an unbounded Vec<String> with no max_items cap and no try_reserve.
findings.failure_mode: A single enormous line (or many lines) can allocate arbitrary heap memory, enabling OOM attacks on untrusted input.
findings.fix: Accept a max_items parameter, validate each line count against it, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| PacketError::Allocation)? before the loop, and enforce the cap before pushing.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() splits and allocates all fields when only two are needed.
findings.failure_mode: Creates intermediate Vec<String> for every line (unnecessary allocation), and any extra commas create extra unused entries rather than a clean two-field parse.
findings.fix: Use let (name, value) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(PacketError::Invalid("missing comma"))?; then parse name.trim() and value.trim().

findings.problem: File I/O (fs::read_to_string), console I/O (println!), parsing, and domain construction are all fused in one function.
findings.failure_mode: Violates Functional Core / Imperative Shell. The pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation. Side effects make the function non-deterministic and untestable.
findings.fix: Split into: (1) shell fn load_packets(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError> handling I/O, (2) pure fn parse_records(lines: &[str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError> with no I/O.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for this crate.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify performance claims or allocation behavior. Unbounded Vec allocation per line may be acceptable but unmeasured.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring throughput and peak heap allocation for realistic input sizes.

findings.failure_mode: Cannot confirm the crate compiles cleanly under strict lint gates required by the Holzman Rust verification gate.
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy with strict gates, and cargo test to produce command evidence.
